name: IN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 point partisan lean
Incumbent Jim Baird running with large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Democratic challenger Drew Cox raised only about $20,000
Prediction markets price Baird at roughly 94% to win
model.rationale: The district's -15 point Republican lean, Baird's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage over a barely funded challenger point to a safe Republican hold, and markets agree at about 94% Republican. No polls or expert ratings exist, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, but nothing suggests movement toward the Democrat.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or a surge in outside spending against Baird would warrant moving this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Western Indiana's fourth district is firmly Republican territory, and Jim Baird is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency. He has raised roughly $358,000 and benefits from more than half a million dollars in outside support, while Democrat Drew Cox has raised only about $20,000 with no outside help. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Baird about a 94% chance of winning.

The fundamentals strongly favor the Republican side: the district leans fifteen points Republican, and the incumbent's financial edge is decisive. Barring an unexpected scandal or a dramatic shift in the national environment, this seat is expected to remain in Republican hands comfortably in November.
